source.snippet: For a site with a clean technical setup, valid XML sitemaps, and a strong internal linking structure, what factors have the most influence on how quickly Google discovers and crawls a newly published URL? How significant are factors such as internal PageRank, URL depth, sitemap lastmod, historical crawl patterns, and external links? Is there a reliable way to distinguish slow crawl prioritization from a technical indexing issue using Google Search Console or server logs?

problem_statement: Website operators and SEO professionals cannot reliably distinguish slow Google crawl prioritization from actual technical indexing failures, leading to wasted diagnostic time and delayed content performance — they need clearer tooling or signals to diagnose crawl vs. index gaps.
target_segment: SEO managers and technical SEO consultants at content-heavy websites, e-commerce stores, and digital agencies
notes: Operator is clearly business-oriented (XML sitemaps, internal PageRank, GSC). Pain is real but Google Search Console tooling gap is well-known; existing tools like Screaming Frog, Sitebulb, and IndexNow partially address this. Opportunity may lie in a specialized crawl-vs-index diagnostic layer on top of GSC log data. Needs more signals to justify building.
